glosses: To pay (a debt or the lender) so as to provide the entire amount of money owed.

examples.text:
Douglas: Roy, give me £20.
Roy: What?
Douglas: Give me £20. I'll pay you back.
He paid her back with interest, giving her ₿3 and an NFT for the $6 he'd borrowed last week.
He paid back all the money he owed her, with interest.
He paid her back with interest, avenging his father's murder with nine degrees of reprisal.

glosses: Synonym of pay back in all senses.

examples.text: I finally repaid my student loans, just before sending my kids to college.
But drops of Grief can ne’re repay / The debt of Love I owe, […]
On the results of the Kent Coast electrification, which is known to be repaying so far a satisfactory return on the investment in it, a Waterloo-Bournemouth scheme shows reasonable financial promise.

glosses: To make worthwhile; to yield a result worth the effort; to pay off.

examples.text: The possible importance of excessive androgen secretion and the ingestion of agents such as the fluorenamines may repay further investigation.

glosses: To pay (cover with tar, pitch, etc.) again.
